title: Linking through unique identifier in location history
description: Location history data stored in DS1 may contain unique identifiers (user IDs, device IDs) that can be used to link data records to specific individuals.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in location history
description: Location history data contains multiple attributes (timestamps, locations) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, enabling re-identification when combined with other data sources.

title: Profiling an individual through location patterns
description: Location history patterns can be analyzed to profile individuals, revealing habits, routines, and sensitive information about their movements.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system processes location history data which is identified personal data, directly linking to specific data subjects.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location data contains revealing attributes (home/work locations, frequent destinations) that support identification of the data subject.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Location history is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required for the map/history view functionality.

title: Excessive volume of location history
description: Full historical location data may be stored and processed beyond what is functionally needed for displaying a map/history view.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and analysis
description: Location data may be further analyzed, enriched, or transformed beyond what is necessary to achieve the map/history view functionality.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Location history data is made accessible to the Mobile App Backend (P1), which may be more parties than functionally necessary.

title: Unawareness of location history processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being retrieved and processed by the backend to serve the map/history view.

title: Lack of control over location data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location history is processed and displayed.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location history may violate GDPR data minimization principle if more personal data is processed than actually needed for the map/history view functionality.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Location history may be stored longer than functionally needed, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.

title: Linking through unique identifier
description: The child's location data can be linked to the child through unique identifiers (e.g., user ID, device ID) that are transmitted with the location information.
assumptions: The system uses identifiers to track the child across sessions and devices.

title: Quasi-identifier combining data
description: Location data combined with other attributes (time, location patterns, family relationships) can serve as quasi-identifiers to uniquely identify the child.
assumptions: Location data is combined with metadata about when and where the child is located.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system requests and processes identified location data of the child, which is personal data that directly identifies the child.
assumptions: The child's location is explicitly tracked and processed by the Mobile App Backend.

title: Identifier in data
description: The location data contains unique references to the child's identity through associated user accounts or device identifiers.
assumptions: Location data is tied to specific user accounts that identify the child.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: Location data is highly sensitive personal data that reveals the child's movements, routines, and whereabouts, which may be more sensitive than functionally required.
assumptions: Location data is considered sensitive under privacy regulations.

title: Data propagation to secondary parties
description: Location data is propagated to secondary guardians (grandparents, relatives) who may not need access to this sensitive information.
assumptions: The parent shares location data with multiple secondary guardians beyond what is functionally necessary.

title: Dynamic set of parties
description: The parties with whom location data is shared are determined dynamically (secondary guardians can be added/removed), creating uncertainty about who has access.
assumptions: Parents can invite different secondary guardians at different times.

title: Unawareness as data subject
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their location data is being shared with secondary guardians.
assumptions: Children may not understand the implications of location sharing with relatives.

title: Lack of control over preferences
description: The child lacks control over who can view their location data and for how long.
assumptions: Children cannot set preferences or consent to location sharing with secondary guardians.

title: Lack of control over rectification/erasure
description: The child may not be able to request removal of their location data from secondary guardians once shared.
assumptions: Data retention policies may not allow easy deletion of shared location data.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Location data may be processed beyond what is functionally needed for the stated purpose of allowing secondary guardians to view the child's location.
assumptions: The system may collect or process more location data than necessary for the intended functionality.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's live location data can be linked to a specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking and association of location data with individual identity.
assumptions: Location data is associated with identifiable user accounts or devices

title: Profiling an individual through location data
description: Live location data can be analyzed to profile a child's movements, routines, and patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily activities and whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data is collected over time and can be analyzed for patterns

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system processes identified personal data (child's live location) which directly reveals the identity and whereabouts of the data subject.
assumptions: Location data is tied to identifiable individuals

title: Data Propagation to External Analytics Partner
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics are propagated from the mobile app backend to an external advertising/analytics partner (EE4) beyond what may be strictly necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The analytics partner may use this data for purposes beyond funding the free tier, potentially expanding data exposure.

title: Predetermined External Data Recipient
description: Personal data is shared with a predetermined set of external parties (advertising/analytics partner) that may not be functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The advertising partner is a known third party, and data sharing with them may exceed functional necessity.

title: User Unawareness of Analytics Data Sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their usage and engagement analytics are being collected and shared with external advertising/analytics partners.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into what data is being shared with third parties for analytics purposes.

title: Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: More personal data (usage and engagement analytics) may be processed and shared than is actually needed to achieve the functional goal of funding the app's free tier.
assumptions: The volume and granularity of analytics data shared may exceed what is strictly necessary for the stated purpose.

title: Potential Invalid Consent for Analytics Data Processing
description: Personal data collection and processing for analytics sharing may not rely on valid consent from data subjects.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms for third-party analytics sharing may be unclear, bundled, or not freely given.

title: Quasi-Identifier Re-identification Risk in Aggregated Analytics
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics may contain combinations of attributes that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individual users when combined with external data.
assumptions: Aggregation may not be sufficiently robust to prevent re-identification through quasi-identifier analysis.
uncertainty_note: Confidence depends on the actual aggregation methodology and data granularity.

title: Quasi-identifiers in Analytics Data
description: The analytics data may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., usage patterns, engagement metrics) that are unique to a data subject, making individuals identifiable despite aggregation.
assumptions: Usage and engagement patterns may be distinctive enough to identify individuals in small user populations.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the size of the user base and the granularity of the analytics.
